title: Infection of Unknown Origin → Septic Shock — Gut Translocation Post-Bowel Resection

patient.name: Robert Klein
patient.procedure: POD2 s/p partial colectomy (bowel resection) for colon adenocarcinoma; TPN initiated POD1; NPO x5 days total (preoperative bowel rest + postoperative ileus)

stages.label: Baseline — POD2, subtle infection signs
stages.facilitatorNotes: On TPN since POD1, ileus, NPO x5 days total. Vitals are nearly normal-looking — HR 98, low-grade temp 37.9 — easy to write off as 'just post-op.' Chart Review/Labs shows lactate 2.1 (mildly elevated, easy to miss). This is the point: nothing screams sepsis yet.

stages.label: Stage II — R/O Sepsis, Evolving SIRS

successCriteria.label: Obtained blood cultures (peripheral + TPN line) before starting antibiotics
Investigated TPN line as a possible source
Identified gut/ileus-translocation as the likely source

stages.facilitatorNotes: Correct moves: blood cultures from BOTH a peripheral site and the TPN line before antibiotics, prompt broad-spectrum empiric coverage, recheck lactate. This is the differential moment — the TPN line is a real, reasonable suspect (running since POD1); coach the learner toward actually investigating it rather than anchoring on the gut source immediately. Chart Review/Labs: lactate trending 2.1 → 3.4, WBC trending up. Not yet a large fluid bolus — lactate's only mildly elevated, this isn't frank shock.

stages.label: Facilitator checkpoint — was the sepsis bundle managed appropriately?

branches.label: Bundle completed promptly — cultures before antibiotics, empiric coverage started, source appropriately investigated
Bundle delayed/incomplete — antibiotics delayed, cultures missed, or source not pursued

stages.facilitatorNotes: Pick based on what actually happened at the bedside — this isn't timed, it's your call as the facilitator.

stages.label: Stabilizing — Bundle-Concordant Management

successCriteria.label: Achieved hemodynamic stabilization before progression to overt shock

stages.facilitatorNotes: Chart Review/Labs: lactate clearing, 3.4 → 1.8. Once settled, manually advance to the debrief discussion when ready — no auto-advance, let it breathe.

stages.label: Septic Shock — Delayed/Incomplete Bundle
stages.facilitatorNotes: Classic warm/distributive shock — SVR frankly low, CO still up, ScvO2 paradoxically high. Chart Review/Labs: lactate 5.8. This meets criteria for a real fluid bolus now (not held back like Stage 2) plus norepinephrine as first-line pressor. Stops here — no scripted progression to arrest for this case. Manually advance to the debrief discussion once managed.

stages.label: Debrief — Source Control Timing
stages.prompt: Whether this settled with early bundle-concordant care or progressed to septic shock, the underlying gut source hasn't been surgically addressed. What's the plan for source control — back to the OR, or managed medically first? How does that timing change once cultures speciate? And what's the plan for the TPN line, now that a gut source has been identified?
stages.note: Source control (per Surviving Sepsis Campaign framing): as soon as medically/logistically feasible, ideally within hours of starting resuscitation, once the patient can tolerate it. Antibiotic de-escalation: narrow once cultures speciate (gram-negative rods/anaerobes typical of gut flora would fit this case). TPN line: peripheral + line cultures work together to rule the line in or out — if line cultures return negative and the gut source is confirmed, there's no indication to pull a working line. Good prompt for the learner: what would change your answer if TPN line cultures came back positive instead?
